items.titulo: Amazon faces study saying 29% of 351 holiday 'deals' were no cheaper
items.resumen: UGG boots sold as a Cyber Monday deal cost 83% more than 27 days before the sale, in a test of 351 products. Amazon says 98% passed. Why do the counts differ?

items.titulo: Heineken campaign returned £2.92 per £1 invested, Mobsta says
items.resumen: Put 40% above a benchmark Mobsta does not name, the result anchors a tool that lets brands weight audience signals by goal. What does the £2.92 figure measure?

items.titulo: Plumbing, not intelligence: Index Exchange on what MCP means for buyers
items.resumen: For media buyers, a stalled deal is the example: an agent checks four bid-funnel points and a human approves a fix. Does Index Exchange run its own MCP server?

items.titulo: AI agents can now pay AWS Marketplace sellers per request, in dollars
items.resumen: Developers' agents get five-minute payment tokens and a $10,000 cap per payment, with Tavily among first sellers. How much AWS keeps per sale is not published.

items.titulo: Microsoft says its bidding upgrade started in summer, not November 18
items.resumen: Advertisers keep Max CPC through portfolio bidding, and five account-level conversions unlock conversion bids, Navah Hopkins says. What did each figure measure?

items.titulo: Semrush puts a number on the visits that begin with an AI answer
items.resumen: US and UK marketers get topic reports built on 29 billion keywords and 317 million AI prompts. Can a modeled estimate show what AI search visibility is worth?

items.titulo: Ad code is no shield: Google's back button spam rule hits the page
items.resumen: Pages reached from Discover or from social media now fall squarely under the June 15 rule, while app hand-offs do not. Where does that leave ad partners' code?

items.titulo: APG|SGA wins 193 more Zurich poster sites under five-year city licences
items.resumen: ShopVille's 23 faces under Zurich Main Station, 13 of them screens, also stay with the Swiss firm. Licences start in February 2027 and can be booked today.

items.titulo: Character.ai says blocking its $10m bidder a day before bids protects no one
items.resumen: Regulators, creditors and the US Trustee hold the New York fund's name in private. Today's hearing decides if a $10m floor lasts to the December 1 auction.

items.titulo: 80% of UK Black Friday shoppers buy from unfamiliar stores, Criteo finds
items.resumen: 42% of 10,500 shoppers would use an AI assistant to choose a gift, 40% are open to it. Criteo pairs that with a 1.5x AI conversion figure measured in February.

items.titulo: Lufthansa Group licenses Platform 195 software for 72-touchpoint ad network
items.resumen: Lounge screens move onto the new system for advertisers in December. Wi-Fi portal ads follow as 850 aircraft go online by 2029. Measurement is still unstated.

items.titulo: Big Tech's tax payments drop to 12.3% of profit, Fair Tax report finds
items.resumen: Meta now ranks worst of six US tech giants, and a UK group says Europe missed out on about $110bn of tax in a decade. Will the EU, the UK or Congress act on it?

items.titulo: Google documents 12 existing bots that ignore robots.txt
items.resumen: Code matching the old APIs-Google string misses a new semicolon, and its push requests skip robots.txt. Which bot renders pages for Google Ads quality checks?

items.titulo: Fewer yeses, no more noes: EU cookie consent falls to 65.2%
items.resumen: TAGGRS data on 17.4bn GA4 events: refusals fell to 12.6% while unrecorded choices rose to 9.7%. Is the missing consent a banner problem, not a visitor one?

items.titulo: Only 8% of managers can make seven core decisions alone, Enhancv finds
items.resumen: Just 7.8% of 65,838 US resumes show an executive title, reached after a median 10 years of work. Does a manager title still mark who signs off on spending?

items.titulo: Dining out would be the first cut for 29% of Americans, Edible poll finds
items.resumen: Just 5% would cut celebrations first, while 52% expect to spend less on dining out or takeout within a year. What the Harris survey of 2,003 adults cannot show.

items.titulo: Amazon blocks third-party Victoria's Secret sellers from November 26
items.resumen: Only accounts holding the Brand Representative role keep selling the lingerie brand. Removals spare Account Health, and the cutoff lands on Thanksgiving Day.

items.titulo: AWS's Garman says AI safety can't hang on an emergency brake
items.resumen: Agents should get their own identity type and no more access than the humans running them, the AWS chief writes a week before re:Invent. What does he leave out?

items.titulo: Google Search asks for the wallet, after the inbox and the photo album
items.resumen: Spending and card perks can now shape AI Mode answers for users who opt in, with Drive and Gemini chats to follow. Will the same data reach the ads beside them?

items.titulo: Three of five Google Photos holiday updates were already available
items.resumen: New today: 12 Remix templates and a people-and-pets filter for shared albums. Gemini, Collections and Fujifilm items predate it. Who can use the new tools?

items.titulo: Disney+ turns the Avengers: Doomsday trailer into a ticket counter
items.resumen: QR codes, phone alerts and Pause Ads send US subscribers to Fandango on TV, mobile and web. Can a streaming app now sell the night out as well as the night in?

items.titulo: DISH Media sells Sling TV ads through Nexxen to reach regional agencies
items.resumen: Live sports and TV series on DISH and Sling reach Nexxen's buyers, with metadata in the bidstream. Which signals that metadata carries is the open question.

items.titulo: Amazon agrees to buy Decart's AI chip software in a deal reported at $7.5bn
items.resumen: Decart's three co-founders are set to join Amazon's Trainium chip effort after Anthropic quit $6bn talks. Amazon discloses no price. What is it really buying?

items.titulo: YouTube adds 15 firms to its Creator Partnerships API
items.resumen: Traackr, GRIN, iKala and Cafe24 join the vendors brands use to reach YouTube's own creator audience data. Two of the 15 surfaced months ago - so what is new?

items.titulo: Platforms face fines up to 1% of global turnover under French press pay law
items.resumen: Arcom can set what platforms pay French publishers after three months of failed talks. Could a free licence in Meta's paused terms leave it nothing to price?

items.titulo: Pinterest sells feed and search ad space through Microsoft Advertising
items.resumen: Microsoft buyers can bid on home feed, search and related Pins in North America, Australia and New Zealand. Europe is left out for the second time in a month.

items.titulo: Half the homes Samba and OpenX reached online missed the TV ads
items.resumen: Lightest-viewing third of homes took 3% of linear TV impressions and nearly 30% of digital ones across 11 campaigns. Missing: spend, dates and a control group.

items.titulo: Texas no longer asks court to make Character.ai name its $10m buyer's backer
items.resumen: Eight limits on Texans' chats, minors' data and ad opt-outs survive the rewrite, which also joins 42 states and DC. Will the December sale order adopt them?

items.titulo: Google Documents Previously Undocumented Crawlers & Fetchers
items.resumen: Google has updated a few of its help documents to add what it calls "additional existing crawlers and user-triggered fetchers." The existing, previously undocumented, Google crawlers and fetchers include Google-analytics-postbacks, Google-Calendar-Importer, GoogleDocs, Google-Edu, pageburst, PlayStore-Google, AppEngine-Google, Google-Apps-Script, Google-Cloud-Tasks, GoogleImageProxy, Google Web Preview, and Chrome-Lighthouse.

items.titulo: Google: Connect Apps To Search In Return For Personal Responses
items.resumen: Robby Stein, VP of Product, Google Search, posted on the Google blog A more tailored Google Search that's uniquely yours. In short, he said he wants you to "connect more of your apps to Personal Intelligence" so that Google AI Mode can provide a "more tailored Google Search."

items.titulo: Custom Attribution Setup in Events Manager
items.resumen: You can now set up custom attribution… Meta announced custom attribution recently as a way to provide different options for how conversions are reported. If you use a third-party analytics partner, in particular, this could prove useful. How to Set It Up Within the Settings tab of Events Manager, you may see a new section... Read more » The post Custom Attribution Setup in Events Manager appeared first on Jon Loomer Digital .

items.titulo: Google Posts FAQs on Back Button Hijacking Spam
items.resumen: Google has added an FAQs section on the back button hijacking spam policy within the spam policies document. Currently, there are five questions and answers in this document and they include:

items.titulo: The Final Ad Checklist Before BFCM – What To Fix Now & What To Leave via @sejournal, @tonyadam
items.resumen: Keep Black Friday ads running with final checks on budgets, purchase tracking, billing, and offers before the holiday rush. The post The Final Ad Checklist Before BFCM – What To Fix Now & What To Leave appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.titulo: Daily Search Forum Recap: November 23, 2026
items.resumen: Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today, through the eyes of the Search Engine Roundtable and other search forums on the web. Google has something it calls StarSearch...

items.titulo: First Impression Ads
items.resumen: This could end badly… A few weeks ago, Meta announced the test of a feature in the US called First Impression Ads. This allows advertisers to book the first ad people see in their feeds. Understand that this isn’t some new ad unit that will look any different or a new placement. It’s not new... Read more » The post First Impression Ads appeared first on Jon Loomer Digital .

items.titulo: AI Needs To Cite Its Sources. This Consumer Intelligence Platform Ensures It Does
items.resumen: Stravito uses a variety of data sources to build out AI personas for different audiences, and touts a “glass box” approach to AI. The post AI Needs To Cite Its Sources. This Consumer Intelligence Platform Ensures It Does appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Ireland's DPC delayed or cancelled 9 AI launches in five years of reviews
items.resumen: Transparency gaps ran through 72% of recommendations to Meta, Google, OpenAI and peers. Next test: AI trained on private messages, which faces a far higher bar.

items.titulo: Google Ads Purchase Signal Annotations Documentation
items.resumen: Google has published a new Google Ads help document on purchase signal annotations. That is the feature you sometimes see in the search ads that have labels like "100+ sold last 30 days." These are aimed at highlighting ads with high-demand items by showcasing purchase volume.

items.titulo: You Can Connect ChatGPT Business Hub With ChatGPT Ad Account
items.resumen: Did you know that you can connect your ChatGPT Ads account in your new ChatGPT Business Hub? There is a button at the top of the ChatGPT Business Hub that says, "Connect an ad account," and adds, "This will let you promote your business and reach more customers across ChatGPT."

items.titulo: The Trade Desk Can Win Again By Embracing Objectivity And Letting Go Of The Open Web
items.resumen: Wall Street loves to pile on ad tech. They’re all about you when you’re up and quick to dismiss you when you’re down. No company has felt the highs and lows of being public quite like The Trade Desk (TTD), which, outside of AppLovin and the Magnificent 7, is the best company to emerge from […] The post The Trade Desk Can Win Again By Embracing Objectivity And Letting Go Of The Open Web appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Adding ASINs to an Amazon brand restates the previous 28 days of data
items.resumen: Advertisers adding ASINs wait 4 to 7 business days for approval, then three weeks of corrections. Bulk tags for Google and Facebook ads can hinge on that wait.

items.titulo: OpenAI's agents finish 46% of long tasks as Ireland logs 9 halted AI launches
items.resumen: OpenAI said its agents finish 46% of two-to-four-hour tasks, Ireland's regulator logged nine halted AI launches and Turkey told Google to free news publishers.

items.titulo: Mark Williams-Cook's joke cats.txt passed four tests used to sell llms.txt
items.resumen: GPTBot crawled it, Google indexed it, an AI Overview cited it and ChatGPT backed it: the signs cited for llms.txt. What would real proof of a GEO tactic need?

items.titulo: Why Mobile Apps Treasure Downtime; Terms Of Non-Endearment
items.resumen: Why don’t more apps double as mobile games?; OpenAI is already tweaking ChatGPT’s business hub; and Bending Spoons is building an army. The post Why Mobile Apps Treasure Downtime; Terms Of Non-Endearment appeared first on AdExchanger .

items.titulo: Google Search Profiles Is Rolling Out Globally
items.resumen: Google seems to have rolled out Search Profiles globally, this has not yet been announced but now folks outside of the United States, Canada and India can now claim their profile without having to go through VPNs to pretend they are in those countries.

items.titulo: Google Ads surcharges hit 3% in France and Italy from January 2027
items.resumen: Turkey's rate halves to 2.25% as Italy rises from 2.5% and France from 2%, billed by where ads are served. What the invoice shows and what Google won't refund.

items.titulo: Google AI Mode Dive Deeper Is Now Live
items.resumen: Several weeks ago, Google announced an update to AI Mode named "Dive deeper." Dive deeper makes the "links that we show at the end of some AI responses more engaging and prominent, with image thumbnails and a more clickable design," Google wrote. And now it seems to be live in AI Mode, not just Google Discover.

items.titulo: Bing Reverting Naming AI Overviews Back To Copilot Search
items.resumen: A couple of months ago, Microsoft renamed the Copilot Search answer box in Bing Search to AI Overviews and has been using the AI Overviews in its blog posts and communications since. But now, Bing is also testing reverting that and going back to using Copilot Answers instead of using AI Overviews.

items.titulo: ChatGPT Product Results May Now Be Influenced By OpenAI Partnerships
items.resumen: OpenAI updated its Shopping with ChatGPT Search help documentation to update the line that says "Product results are selected independently by ChatGPT and are not ads, nor influenced by any OpenAI partnerships." It now says, "Product results are not ads; how products and merchants are selected is described below." In short, OpenAI removed the disclaimer that these shopping results are independent of and not influenced by any OpenAI partnerships.

items.titulo: Google Search Profiles With LinkedIn Support
items.resumen: Google has made it easier to manage your LinkedIn profile in Google Search Profiles by adding it as an option to the list of social network platforms that you can connect. Previously, Google would automatically add LinkedIn to Search Profiles on its own but now you can try to add it manually if you want.

items.titulo: Google blocks 41 AI crawlers from Maps in its own robots.txt
items.resumen: GPTBot, ClaudeBot and 39 other bots now sit under the AI training opt-out Google backed in October, while its own Gemini control stays outside. Why the split?

items.titulo: Google StarSearch, AIGC, Zero-History Discovery, Feed Ranking & More
items.resumen: Google has posted a new job listing for a Senior Software Engineer, Discover Feed Recommendations. And in that job listing, it lists a number of interesting Google Search tidbits, including something called "StarSearch," as well as AIGC, Zero-History Discovery, Feed Ranking, and more.

items.titulo: Bing Thanksgiving Turkey Trot In Search Results
items.resumen: Microsoft Bing has a cute easter egg when you search for Thanksgiving in the Bing Search results. A turkey crosses the screen as leaves fall from the trees.

items.titulo: Blade Runner 2099 arrives November 25 with all 8 episodes in 240 markets
items.resumen: Ads run by default on US Prime Video, where the Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer series lands Thanksgiving eve. What did Alcon tell a court about car brands?

items.titulo: Prime Video sets December 5 for 14-episode Korean epic Sacred Jewel
items.resumen: Thailand, the one market Amazon names, is missing from its list of 20 Prime Video ad markets. Who pays for a K-drama set in 1258 when it streams in Bangkok?

items.titulo: Amazon routes new Brand Store pages through an AI agent first
items.resumen: Brand owners get six starter prompts and output fixed to one language, while an All Deals tab fills itself. Can agent-built pages clear Amazon's moderation?

items.titulo: Campaign bid strategy
items.resumen: Campaign bid strategy is the Amazon Ads reporting field naming the bidding rule on a Sponsored Products campaign, such as fixed or dynamic bids, on each row.

items.titulo: Ad group bid strategy
items.resumen: Ad group bid strategy is the Amazon Ads reporting field naming the bidding priority set on an ad group, the DVA+ unit once called a line item in Amazon DSP.

items.titulo: Ad group optimization type
items.resumen: Ad group optimization type is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field that records the KPI a Sponsored Display ad group optimises for: reach, visits or sales.

items.titulo: Campaign rule amount
items.resumen: Campaign rule amount is an Amazon Ads unified reporting dimension showing a campaign budget after a budget rule raises it for a schedule or performance trigger.

items.titulo: Campaign cost type
items.resumen: Campaign cost type is an Amazon Ads unified reporting dimension naming the unit a campaign is billed on, such as cost per click, vCPM, CPM or a fixed price.

items.titulo: Ad group cost type
items.resumen: Ad group cost type is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field naming how an ad group is billed: per click, per viewable thousand or per thousand impressions.

items.titulo: Ad group delivery status
items.resumen: Ad group delivery status is the Amazon Ads unified report field showing whether an ad group, the unit that replaced the DSP line item, can serve or why not.

items.titulo: Ad group budget amount
items.resumen: Ad group budget amount is an Amazon Ads unified reporting dimension giving the money set on one DVA+ ad group, the former line item, below its campaign budget.

items.titulo: Flight budget
items.resumen: Flight budget is an Amazon Ads unified reporting dimension showing the money set for one dated flight in a DVA campaign, the slice Amazon paces spend toward.

items.titulo: Flight start date
items.resumen: Flight start date is an Amazon Ads unified reporting dimension giving the day a DVA campaign flight begins delivery, the point from which its budget is paced.

items.titulo: Flight end date
items.resumen: Flight end date is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field showing when a flight, a dated budget period inside a DVA+ campaign, stops spending its set budget.

items.titulo: Flight ID
items.resumen: Flight ID is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field identifying a flight, a dated budget period inside a DVA+ campaign, used to track spend window by window.

items.titulo: Flight name
items.resumen: Flight name is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field showing the label given to a flight, a dated budget period inside a DVA+ campaign, so reports read clearly.

items.titulo: Ad group start date
items.resumen: Ad group start date is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field showing when an ad group was scheduled to begin delivery, the DSP line item start in new form.

items.titulo: Ad group end date
items.resumen: Ad group end date is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field showing when an ad group, the unit that replaced the DSP line item, is set to stop serving ads.

items.titulo: Ad group language targeting
items.resumen: Ad group language targeting is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field showing the language rule set on a DVA+ ad group, the unit formerly called a line item.

items.titulo: Ad group type
items.resumen: Ad group type is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field that labels what kind of ad group a DVA+ row came from, the role the old DSP line item type once played.

items.titulo: Ad group name
items.resumen: Ad group name is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field holding the editable label of an ad group, replacing the DSP "Line item name" column for DVA+ buys.

items.titulo: Ad ID
items.resumen: Ad ID is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field holding the fixed system identifier of an individual ad, merging DSP "Creative ID" and sponsored ads "Ad ID".

items.titulo: Campaign country
items.resumen: Campaign country is the Amazon Ads unified report field naming the country a campaign is set to deliver in, a campaign setting rather than a measure of reach.

items.titulo: Campaign PO number
items.resumen: Campaign PO number is an optional Amazon Ads reporting field holding the buyer's purchase order reference for a campaign, used to tie spend to client invoices.

items.titulo: Ad group OMS ID
items.resumen: Ad group OMS ID is an Amazon Ads unified reporting field carrying the order management system reference for a DVA+ ad group, tying delivery to a sold line.

items.titulo: Ad group comments
items.resumen: Ad group comments is the Amazon Ads unified reporting field holding free-text notes a buyer writes on a DVA+ ad group, exported alongside its delivery data.
